content.title: Michigan State basketball falls short to UConn 67-63 in Sweet 16
content.text: March 27, 2026Updated March 28, 2026, 12:25 a.m. ETMichigan State basketball almost completed an impressive comeback, but ultimately fell to a higher seed in the NCAA Tournament.The 3-seed Spartans lost 67-63 to the 2-seed UConn Huskies in the East Regional semifinals of the 2026 NCAA Tournament on Friday, March 27, at Capital One Arena in Washington. UConn senior Alex Karaban led all scorers with 20 points and added five rebounds, four assists and two blocks in an all-around performance.With the win, UConn advances to the Elite Eight and will play the 1-seed Duke Blue Devils on Sunday, March 30. UConn's defense held Michigan State to just six points over the first 10 minutes of the game and at one point held a 19-point lead over the Spartans, but Michigan State mounted a second-half comeback and at one point took a lead with minutes remaining in the game. Watch NCAA Tournament on FuboHowever, the Huskies made enough clutch shots down the stretch to end the Spartans' season.The Spartans were looking to make their second consecutive Elite Eight appearance in their 28th consecutive NCAA tournament trip under coach Tom Izzo. It was Dan Hurley's squad who emerged victorious, however, with the Spartans now in offseason mode.Here's how it all went down. UConn beats Michigan State, advance to Elite EightFINAL: UConn 67, Michigan State 63.It truly was an impressive comeback for the Spartans, at one point down by 19 points to the 2-seed Huskies. But UConn held on with key baskets late in the game to survive its Sweet 16 matchup.Michigan State men's basketball's season comes to an end. Tarris Reed makes it a 4-point game for UConn2H, 0:04: UConn 67, MSU 63.Michigan State center Carson Cooper missed his second free throw, possibly intentionally, with UConn big man Tarris Reed Jr. getting the rebound and immediately drawing a foul. He then made both free throws, his second bringing him to a game-high 20 points.With only four seconds left and the Huskies up by four points, this game is essentially over. Kur Teng misses potential game-tying 3-pointer2H, 0:04: UConn 65, MSU 63.UConn big man Alex Caraban hit two free throws to once again make it a 3-point game. The Spartans held the ball for a while on their possession and had to shoot a 3-pointer with time winding down, and Kur Teng's contested 3 hit the back of the rim.Center Carson Cooper got the rebound and drew the foul, making his first free throw before UConn called a timeout. It's a 2-point game with four seconds left. Jeremy Fears hits his free throws2H, 0:32: UConn 63, MSU 62.Michigan State point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. found an angle towards the basket and drew a shooting foul to head to the free-throw line. He hit both free throws to make it a one-point UConn lead once again. UConn up by 3 points, less than a minute left2H, 0:41: UConn 63, MSU 60.UConn big man Alex Karaban hit a clutch 3-pointer with less than two minutes left to give the Huskies a 4-point lead, to which Jeremy Fears responded with a 3-pointer of his own to bring the UConn lead back to 1 point with a minute left in the game.UConn forward Tarris Reed Jr. then hit two free throws. It's a 3-point game, and the Spartans will have the ball after the break. Michigan State down by 1 point2H, 1:50: UConn 58, MSU 57.Jeremy Fears' turnover gave UConn the ball in a critical spot, but a smart foul by Fears ended the transition opportunity, and Fears drew a moving screen foul on the next inbound to give Michigan State the ball back. Carson Cooper's dunk then made it a one-point game for the Spartans heading into the timeout. Carson Cooper snaps scoreless drought2H, 3:08: UConn 58, MSU 55.Consecutive layup attempts from Jeremy Fears and Carson Cooper both rimmed out as the Spartans aimed to tie the game. UConn guard Solo Ball took advantage with four consecutive points, while forward Jayden Ross hit a free throw to extend the 10-2 run for UConn.Cooper's two-handed dunk through the lane snapped a more than 3-minute scoreless stretch for the Spartans, while his two made free throws once again made it a one-possession game for Michigan State with four minutes left. Michigan State and UConn trading leads2H, 7:40: UConn 51, MSU 49.Back-to-back buckets from Michigan State big men Coen Carr and Jaxon Kohler tied the game at 44-44, with Kohler's and-one free-throw giving the Spartans a 45-44 lead. It was their first lead of the game since the first minutes of the game.Spartans center Carson Cooper hit a shot to re-take the lead with about nine minutes left in the game, but UConn big man Terris Reed Jr. hit a tough bucket to give UConn the lead back. A 3-pointer from UConn big man Alex Karaban gave the Huskies a 4-point lead, and Michigan State point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. responded with a running layup off the glass before drawing a foul on the floor. Michigan State cuts UConn lead to four points2H, 11:47: UConn 44, MSU 40.Jordan Scott's 3-pointer as the shot clock expired brought the Spartans back to within three points of the Huskies a little more than five minutes into the half. Michigan State attempted to turn good defense into points, but UConn big man Alex Karaban responded with better defense, recording blocks on back-to-back possessions.Trey Fort's 3-pointer cut the UConn lead to two points, only for Karaban's layup to bring it back to four. We have a game. Coen Carr with two highlight-reel plays2H, 15:17: UConn 40, MSU 34.Michigan State center Carson Cooper started the second half with a tough layup through contact, making the and-one free throw to shrink UConn's lead to five points. Two possessions later, Coen Carr found his trampoline to block Tarris Reed Jr's layup attempt and turned the defense into offense with a jump shot off the dribble.Two possessions later, Carr hit a tough layup but couldn't hit the ensuing free throw that would have tied the game. UConn took advantage with a deep two-pointer from Braylon Mullins and a transition dunk from Reed to extend their lead to six points. Michigan State cuts deficit to 8 points at halftimeEnd 1H: UConn 35, MSU 27.A Solo Ball reverse layup ended Michigan State's 7-0 run and gave UConn a 10-point lead, but a response layup from Spartans point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. cut the lead back down to single digits for Michigan State.The good news for the Spartans is that their defense once again looks elite. It's now up to the offense to turn it up in the second half. Bill Murray in the houseLegendary actor Bill Murray was shown on the broadcast wearing a very Chicago hat.Why is he there? We have the story. Michigan State chipping away at UConn lead1H, 2:01: UConn 33, Michigan State 23.A 3-pointer from Michigan State forward Jaxon Kohler brought the Spartans to within 12 points with under three minutes left in the half, while a Coen Carr layup brought the deficit to 11 points. UConn calls timeout after the 5-0 Spartans run. Jeremy Fears gets involved1H, 3:09: UConn 33, MSU 18.A swipe from Michigan State point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. led to a transition bucket to cut UConn's lead to 13 points. It was UConn's first turnover of the game.A few possessions later, Fears found center Carson Cooper for an alley-oop, marking his first assist of the game. But the Huskies responded to both buckets with buckets of their own, stifling the positive momentum the Spartans looked like they were generating. Michigan State still down by 15. Michigan State falls even further behind1H, 7:12: UConn 27, MSU 12.Things have only gotten worse for the Spartans.Michigan State scored only six points in the first 10 minutes of the game while allowing the Huskies on a 100-point pace. A Coen Carr layup finally snapped a nine-minute drought in which the Spartans did not hit a field goal, while UConn's 21-2 run has opened up the game for the 2-seed Huskies.There is still plenty of time for the Spartans to come back, but with it getting so ugly this early, that comeback is going to have to start soon. After all, the Spartans only have 12 points after 13 minutes of play. Michigan State cold from the field1H, 11:58: UConn 18, MSU 6.After taking a 4-0 lead early, the Spartans missed 10 straight shots as they allowed the Huskies to take control of the game.Absolutely nothing is working on offense so far for Michigan State with the Spartans shooting 2-for-13 from the floor. Meanwhile, UConn is shooting 6-for-10 as they take a 12-2 run into the timeout. UConn takes early lead1H, 13:29: UConn 10, MSU 5.UConn has found buckets early against a tough Michigan State defense, taking an early lead in Washington. UConn freshman guard Braylon Mullins leads all scorers with five early points. Duke beats St. John'sTop-seeded Duke held off 5-seed St. John's for an 80-75 win in the Sweet 16. They advance to the Elite Eight to play the winner of the Michigan State-UConn game. Michigan State starting lineupEarly lineups courtesy of our Spartans insider Chris Solari don't show any surprises for Michigan State.F Jaxon Kohler.PG Jeremy Fears Jr.F Jordan Scott.C Carson Cooper.F Coen Carr.What time is Michigan State vs UConn game today in Sweet 16Date: Friday, March 27.Time: 9:45 p.m. ET.Location: Capital One Arena, Washington.What channel is Michigan State vs UConn game on today in Sweet 16Channel: CBS.Tipoff: 9:45 p.m. ET.Streaming: Paramount+, Fubo.Audio: Westwood One Sports.Friday's Sweet 16 game between Michigan State and UConn can be watched on CBS and streamed on Paramount+ and Fubo, which carries CBS.Watch Michigan State-UConn on FuboMichigan State vs UConn odds in March Madness Sweet 16Spread: UConn by 1½ points.Over/under: 136½ points.Moneyline: Michigan State (+110), UConn (-130).All odds courtesy of BetMGM as of Friday afternoon.Michigan State vs UConn prediction for Sweet 16 gameChris Solari, Detroit Free Press: How the Spartans react to another early deficit on their biggest stage of the season will be critical, and Fears once again wills them back by halftime. But the Huskies’ interior depth and strength, particularly Reed’s physicality, gets Kohler, Cooper and Ward into foul trouble and exploits MSU’s thin post rotation. Ultimately, Fears’ stellar performance isn’t enough, and the Spartans’ season ends short of last season’s Elite Eight trip. The pick: UConn 78, MSU 73.Michigan State Sweet 16 appearancesThis is Michigan State's 19th appearance in the Sweet 16 since the NCAA Tournament expanded to 64 teams in 1985, with Tom Izzo accounting for a ridiculous 17 of those. The Spartans of course had been among the final 16 teams before the expansion, including the 1979 season when they won the title with Magic Johnson over Indiana State and Larry Bird.Michigan State NCAA Tournament scoresFirst round: W, 92-67 vs North Dakota State.Second round: W, 77-69 vs Louisville.Sweet Sixteen, March 27: vs 2-seed UConn, 9:45 p.m. ET (CBS).Need to catch up on the news during your lunch break?
